items.memo:
BILL NUMBER:  S557

 TITLE OF BILL :
An act to amend the personal property law, in relation to providing
consumers with greater protection in rental purchase agreements; to
repeal certain provisions of such law relating thereto; and providing
for the repeal of certain provisions upon expiration thereof


 PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL :
The purpose of this bill is to increase consumer protections in the
rent-to-own industry and to provide rent-to-own merchants with
increased regulatory guidance.

 SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS :
This bill would make significant changes to the Rent to Own Program
Law (Article 11 of the Personal Property Law), by providing for
enhanced disclosures and providing for an extensive retail survey that
would serve as the basis for improving the law's price control
provisions and requiring rent-to-own merchants to provide consumers
with enhanced disclosures.

The bill would require rent-to-own merchants to provide consumers with
enhanced disclosures. Specifically, the bill would require rent-to-own
merchants to:

* include a "disclosure box" containing the total amount of payments,
cost of rental, cash price, amount of each payment, number of payments
and the rental period, along with a layman's explanation of the first
three terms on every rental-purchase agreement. This disclosure box
would also be required to be affixed to all merchandise;

* include a notice containing a layman's explanation of the
rental-purchase transaction in each rental agreement;

* provide notice to consumers of the early purchase option, including
the total amount necessary to acquire ownership, on three occasions;
thirty to sixty days before the early purchase option expires, the
date the consumer has made one-half of all payments required to obtain
ownership, and the date a consumer requests information regarding the
amount required to purchase the merchandise; and

* provide customers with a copy of the signed rental-purchase
agreement.

This bill would also require the Consumer Protection Board and the
Department of Economic Development, in consultation with
representatives from the rent-to-own industry, the business
commnunity, and consumer advocates, to perform a survey of retailers
located within the state to determine the average markup applied by
retailers to consumer goods offered for sale to the public for the
purposes of providing the Legislature with the information necessary
to determine a fair formula for rent-to-own merchants to use in
setting cash prices. The Board and the Department would also be
required to make a joint recommendation as to appropriate and fair
formulas for determining cash prices for rent-to-own merchandise to
the Governor and Legislature.

In addition, the bill would:

* provide consumers the right to acquire ownership of the merchandise
within three months of signing an agreement by paying the cash price
minus all payments paid;

* exempt Sundays and federally recognized holidays from the time
periods used to determine late charges or reinstatement fees;
* require rent-to-own merchants to offer customers extended
reinstatement rights and the option of entering into weekly or monthly
leases; and

* require merchants to provide notice of the consumer's right to
reinstate the agreement upon repossession of merchandise.

 JUSTIFICATION :
New York's "Rent to Own Program Law" (Article 11 of the Personal
Property Law) was enacted in 1986 and has not been updated since that
time. The law caps the total amount a consumer must pay in order to
acquire ownership of the merchandise at twice the "cash price" of the
merchandise, which is defined as the price at which the merchant would
sell the merchandise to the consumer for cash.  According to memoranda
issued at the time of the law's enactment, several consumer groups, as
well as Attorney General Robert Abrams, voiced concern that
rent-to-own merchants could abuse their authority to set cash prices.
According to recent reports and testimony received at the September
20, 2006 and October 5, 2006 Assembly public hearings on financial
services for low-income consumers, rent-to-own merchants often
sidestep the intent of the law by setting cash prices as high as twice
the price found for the same merchandise at nearby retail outlets.

This bill would provide for a detailed retail survey which would serve
as the basis for establishing fair and reasonable formulas for
rent-toown merchants to use in determining cash prices. This would
ensure that rent-to-own customers pay fair prices and provide
much-needed regulatory guidance to merchants, by removing any
uncertainty concerning the setting of cash prices. This bill would
also significantly strengthen existing law by implementing several new
and enhanced consumer disclosures. For example, rent-to-own merchants
would be required to include a disclosure box containing important
information for consumers, similar to the Schumer Box currently
required to be included in credit card solicitations.

This legislation recognizes that rent-to-own merchants provide a
unique transaction utilized by many consumers. This bill would ensure
that consumers are aware of their rights and obligations prior to
entering into a rent-to-own agreement. The bill would also provide the
Legislature with the retail pricing data necessary to establish
reasonable price controls. California recently updated the cash price
formulas contained in its rent-to-own law using such data. This
pragmatic approach to price controls will ensure that consumers pay
reasonable prices, while allowing the rent-to-own industry to continue
to offer its unique product in New York state.

 PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :
2007: A.66-B - Referred to Codes
2005-2006:  A.230 - Referred to Consumer Affairs and Protection
2003-2004: A.3511 - Referred to Consumer Affairs and Protection
2001-2002: A.401B - Referred to Consumer Affairs and Protection

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS :
Minimal.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect on the one hundred eightieth day after it
shall have become a law and shall apply to all agreements entered into
or offered on or after such date; provided, however, that section
eight of this act shall take effect immediately and shall expire and
be deemed repealed March 1, 2010.

C.memo:
BILL NUMBER:S557C

TITLE OF BILL:
An act
to amend the personal property law, in relation to providing consumers
with greater protection in rental purchase agreements; and
to repeal certain provisions of such law relating thereto

PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:
The purpose of this bill is to
increase consumer protections in the rent-to-own industry and to
provide rent-to-own merchants with increased regulatory guidance.

SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:
This bill would make significant
changes to the Rent to Own Program Law (Article 11 of the Personal
Property Law), most notably by establishing well-defined price
controls and requiring rent-to-own merchants to provide consumers
with enhanced disclosures.

Under current law, the total amount a rent-to-own customer must pay in
order to acquire ownership of the merchandise is limited to twice the
"cash price" of the merchandise, which is defined as the price at
which the merchant would sell the merchandise to the consumer for
cash. This bill would implement a new price control scheme by:

* establishing a formula for determining the maximum cash price for
new goods based on the merchant's actual cost of acquiring the
merchandise;

* establishing a formula for determining the maximum amount a consumer
must pay in order acquire ownership of the merchandise;
and

* providing for the pricing of used merchandise based on a terming
matrix that would allow merchants to consider the condition of the
merchandise.

The bill would require rent-to-own merchants to provide consumers with
enhanced disclosures. Specifically, the bill would require
rent-to-own merchants to:

o include a "disclosure box" containing the total amount of payments,
cost of rental, cash price, amount of each payment, number of
payments and the rental period, along with a layman's explanation of
the first three terms on every rental-purchase agreement. This
disclosure box would also be required to be affixed to all merchandise;

o include a notice containing a layman's explanation of the
rental-purchase transaction in each rental agreement;

o provide notice to consumers of the early purchase option, including
the total amount necessary to acquire ownership or exercise the early
purchase option on each payment receipt; and

o provide customers with a copy of the signed rental-purchase agreement.

In addition, the bill would:

o authorize the Attorney General to promulgate regulations necessary
for the administration of the rent-to-own law;

o require rent-to-own merchants to offer customers extended
reinstatement rights;

o require merchants to provide notice of the consumer's right to
reinstate the agreement upon repossession of merchandise;

o require rent-to-own merchants to maintain rental merchandise in good
working order and provide for repair and replacement of merchandise
that is not operating properly; and

o require merchants to offer consumers that suffer an interruption or
reduction of income the option of paying temporarily reduced rental
payments in certain situations.

JUSTIFICATION:
New York's "Rent to Own Program Law" (Article 11 of the
Personal Property Law) was enacted in 1986 and has not been updated
since that time. The law caps the total amount a consumer must pay in
order to acquire ownership of the merchandise at twice the "cash
price" of the merchandise, which is defined as the price at which the
merchant would sell the merchandise to the consumer for cash.
According to memoranda issued at the time of the law's enactment,
several consumer groups, as well as Attorney General Robert Abrams,
voiced concern that rent-to-own merchants could abuse their authority
to set cash prices.
According to recent reports and testimony received at the September
20, 2006 and October 5, 2006 Assembly public hearings on financial
services for low-income consumers, rent-to-own merchants often
sidestep the intent of the law by arbitrarily setting elevated cash
prices.

This bill would significantly strengthen existing law by implementing
several new and enhanced consumer disclosures. For example,
rent-to-own merchants would be required to include a disclosure box
containing important information for consumers, similar to the
Schumer Box currently required to be included in credit card
solicitations.

This legislation recognizes that rent-to-own merchants provide a
unique transaction utilized by many consumers. This bill would ensure
that consumers are aware of their rights and obligations prior to

entering into a rent-to-own agreement. The bill would also provide
for reasonable price controls in order to ensure that consumers pay
reasonable prices, while allowing the rent-to-own industry to
continue to offer its unique product in New York state.

PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2007-2008: A.66-C - Advanced to Third Reading
2005-2006: A.230  - Referred to Consumer Affairs and Protection
2003-2004: A.3511 - Referred to Consumer Affairs and Protection
2001-2002: A4018  - Referred to Consumer Affairs and Protection

FISCAL IMPLICATIONS FOR STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS:
None to the State.

EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the one hundred
eightieth day after it shall have become a law and shall apply to all
agreements entered into or offered on or after such date.

summary: Provides for greater protections to consumers in rental purchase agreements; defines certain terms; provides greater disclosure to consumer regarding the amount, number and times at which various payments relating to such an agreement are due and owing; makes various provisions regarding the method and information required to be disclosed in advertising for such agreements; provides for a right of reinstatement upon repossession.
